commits.message:
Reduced motion: one switch draws every animation at its rest (rich-animation-42lg.a38) (#492)

* Reduced motion: one switch draws every animation at its rest (rich-animation-42lg.a38)

An Animation now says its rest() — a loop's first value, a one-shot's end —
and every combinator says it once, so a transition rests at its new state, a
lifecycle arrived (or gone once told to leave), a stagger with everyone
arrived. reducedMotion on Console (which a Live draws through), on App, and on
animationFuncs is the one switch; shownAt in core/view.ts is the one place it
is read, by drawView and by every renderable built for the host's time.
drawView takes the render options once and hands them to its draw. Nothing
reads the environment.

Named limit: a text frame a function view splices itself with frameAt, or a
value it samples itself, is its own sample; at rest a function view is asked
at 0. docs/animation.md#reduced-motion says so.

* Reduced motion keeps content on time: an animation reduced is an animation (rich-animation-42lg.a38)

The high review of #492 showed a time-free rest() cannot say when content
shows: a lifecycle told to leave later drew as already gone, and a function
view pinned at view(0) froze the lifecycle demo on its first line.
Animation<T>.rest(): T becomes reduced(): Animation<T> — the motion taken
out, what shows and when kept. Function views are asked at the real t.

Also: a reduced sequence wakes nothing at its switch; drawView's since-when
reads the reduced animation, so a reversed timeline is never told to look
again; renderToString takes reducedMotion; one finiteTime refusal in
core/easing serves every "needs a finite t".

* A reduced sequence keeps both parts on time; a reduced element wakes its host when gone (rich-animation-42lg.a38)

Medium review of #492: sequence is a general combinator, so skipping `first`
dropped content (a loading text before results). It is now each part reduced
with the switch kept; a transition says its own end. A lifecycle reduced shows
nothing once told to leave but still says it changes when `gone`, so a host
pruning on gone(t) drops it on time. The template frames/stepped refuse a
non-finite frameTime() under reduced motion as with motion.

* A one-shot reduced cuts to its end when it starts; a glyph loop reduced is the text as written (rich-animation-42lg.a38)

Escalation review of #492. A reduced tween or transition was its end at every
time, so one scheduled later showed finished early; Animation.cut(before,
after) keeps the start and drops the motion. A stagger reduced has everyone
arrived, its offsets being choreography. caseWave and particles reduced draw
the text as written instead of a band or field frozen at step 0. The scroll
marquee starts from the line so its held loop shows it. CLAUDE.md names
reduced() and the widened held.
